text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government did not reveal suspected ETA guerrilla who died in prison had his hands tied
- SOCCER - Madrid eight points ahead over Barcelona
- All TV will offer football matches 'a la carte' to their subscribers
- Basque church pushed for dialogue between Spain's government and ETA
- Retevision won't be privatised until June
- Low interest rates prompt luxury car purchases
- A report by Galician regional government la Xunta is in favour of mergers among regional saving banks
- Spain will set up new firm to boost its exports. It will be called Expansion Exterior Espanola and will subsitute old Focoex, plagued by scandals.
- Only five out of 18 motorways will be profitable without public aid
- Renfe is looking for private money to fund and up its investments.
- Large Spanish banks expect high profits in Latin America
- Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez-Cascos takes his cheque book out. He has guaranteed regions that capital frozen since the Civil war will be returned to them.
- Labour reform in hands of Labour Minister Javier Arenas
